Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/18/2026
Patient: Mirian Kutch, 74-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Kutch presents for her routine follow-up. She reports no new complaints today and feels generally well. No recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Musculoskeletal exam shows no tenderness or deformities.

Assessment:
Ms. Kutch remains stable with no new issues noted at this visit.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/01/2026
Patient: Mirian Kutch, 74-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/01/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture at L2 with associated bone marrow edema consistent with recent injury.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on the patient's symptoms and overall clinical picture.

notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/11/2026
Patient: Mirian Kutch, 74-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 07/11/2026 after a fall from standing height, 9 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 8 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Management:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Plan:
Continue current pain management and brace use. Monitor symptoms closely. Consider interventional options if pain persists or worsens.
